findings.description: Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in file type validation - os.stat() call after os.path.exists() check allows file substitution between checks
findings.reasoning: The os.stat() call at line 315 follows the os.path.exists() check at line 313. Between these two system calls, an attacker could replace a regular file with a special file (device, FIFO, socket). This defeats the security check intended to prevent operations on special files, as the file could be changed to a special file after the existence check but before the stat call retrieves its type.

evidence.code_context: is_special_file method at lines 300-330 in s3transfer/utils.py checks if a file is a special UNIX file (device, FIFO, socket) to prevent operations on them.
evidence.vulnerability_pattern: TOCTOU race condition: os.path.exists(filename) at line 313 followed by os.stat(filename).st_mode at line 315
evidence.exploitation_scenario: Between the exists check and stat call, file can be replaced with symlink to special file or the file itself can be changed, bypassing the security check
evidence.attack_vector: An attacker with file system access or via a race condition could replace a file between the two system calls to cause unintended operations on special files

flags.message: TOCTOU vulnerability is not practically exploitable in this library context. The function is a local file validation check called during S3 file transfer operations - an attacker who can race-condition replace files on the local filesystem already has the ability to perform any operations they want on that filesystem, making the special file check ineffective as a security boundary.
flags.evidence: s3transfer is a library for transferring files to/from S3; local filesystem race conditions are not within the threat model. Any attacker with capabilities to race-condition local files has already compromised the system.

flags.message: While technically a TOCTOU pattern exists in the code, this is a best-practice issue rather than a practical vulnerability. The check is defensive programming to warn users about special files, not a security boundary. The proper fix (using lstat or open with validation) would be a code quality improvement, not a security patch.
flags.evidence: The function returns a boolean for caller inspection; it doesn't prevent operations, merely identifies file types. The responsibility for preventing operations on special files rests with the caller.

flags.message: s3transfer is a library (integration/infrastructure layer), not a system utility or daemon. The exploitability model for TOCTOU vulnerabilities requires the library to enforce a security boundary, but here the library merely provides information to its caller. The caller bears responsibility for secure file handling.
flags.evidence: Package type: library; Layer: integration, infrastructure. The function is a utility check without enforcement capabilities.

sanity_check.reasoning: While the code does contain a technical TOCTOU pattern (os.path.exists followed by os.stat), this is not a practical security vulnerability in the s3transfer library context. findings.description: Unbounded memory allocation when reading non-seekable file objects in upload operations
findings.reasoning: The UploadNonSeekableInputManager.get_put_object_body() method calls fileobj.read() without any size limits. For non-seekable streams, the size cannot be determined beforehand (as shown in provide_transfer_size() which is a no-op). This means an attacker can provide a malicious stream that is arbitrarily large, causing unbounded memory allocation when the entire stream is read into memory via self._initial_data + fileobj.read(). The concatenation creates a new bytes object in memory containing all the data, which could exhaust available memory.

evidence.code_context: In UploadNonSeekableInputManager class (lines 376-430), the get_put_object_body method reads entire file object without bounds
evidence.dataflow_analysis: fileobj.read() -> concatenated to self._initial_data -> wrapped in self._wrap_data() -> returned as body for upload
evidence.notes: provide_transfer_size() is a no-op for this manager (line 388-390), confirming size cannot be determined for non-seekable streams. The method requires_multipart_upload() reads up to threshold but get_put_object_body reads ALL remaining data unconditionally.

flags.evidence: UploadNonSeekableInputManager is designed for non-seekable streams where size cannot be predetermined. The vulnerability manifests when an untrusted stream source is provided to the library's upload operations.
